name: The Sweep — Cannery Row
description: Two things can be noticed while painting over a dozen cicada stencils: where they are, and what they are made of. Neither is offered. The first is called for once, unprompted, after the fourth wall; the second only if somebody examines the medium.

dc.basis: level 1 standard DC, unadjusted — the information is in plain sight and the only barrier is looking at placement rather than at the stencil

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Every stencil is at head height for a standing adult, on a wall people stand in front of — the tram stop, the labour exchange queue, outside the picture house, the corner where the market spills. And none of them face a road. They all face where people wait.
outcomes.success: Every stencil is at head height. Not eye level for a tall man, not a child's height. And every one is on a wall people stand in front of.
outcomes.failure: It is just graffiti. It is everywhere. It is annoying.

dc.basis: level 1 standard DC nudged one step for an industrial product identified by behaviour rather than by label

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Marine primer — and chandler's stock at that. Three suppliers in the city carry it in quantity, and all three are on the harbour side.
outcomes.success: It is not spray and it is not house paint. It is marine primer, the grey-green they put on hulls below the waterline. It bites into brick and does not come off, which is why municipal grey needs three coats.
outcomes.failure: Paint is paint. It is taking three coats, which is annoying.

participants: Any of the five on the works detail
notes: Neither check costs a wall — noticing is free, acting on it is not. The spends in head-height-docket are what cost.
